connect.title: Connect Expo Go
connect.subtitle: Open your iPhone Camera app and scan this QR code
connect.or: — or enter this URL manually in Expo Go —
connect.steps:
1. Open the Camera app on your iPhone
2. Point it at the QR code above
3. Tap the notification to open in Expo Go

Make sure Expo Go is installed from the App Store.
connect.webNote:
This page is only for connecting Expo Go.
The full app runs on your iPhone.

capture.cameraRequiredDesc: Geospector needs camera access to record GPS-tagged video and photos.

log.title: Frame Log
log.noFramesDesc: Start recording on the Capture tab. Frames are extracted and GPS-tagged automatically every 90 seconds.
log.clearAllDesc: This will permanently delete all captured frames and GPS log data. This cannot be undone.
log.setPortalUrl: Set your Portal URL in Settings before publishing.
log.noDataSubtitle: Capture frames to view them here.
log.jobNameSubtitle: Label this session for easy identification
log.extractingFrames: Extracting frames and associating GPS data...
log.removeFromAtlasDesc: This will permanently remove this session from the public Geospector Atlas feed.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Frame extraction configuration
settings.jobNameHint: Sessions captured while this name is active are grouped under the same project. Visible in the camera HUD.
settings.lockFocusInfinityDesc: Prevents autofocus from locking onto the dashboard or other nearby objects
settings.saveToRollDesc: Each captured photo is also saved to your iPhone Camera Roll
settings.filesHint: GPX tracks and frame data are also accessible via the Files app under Geospector
settings.savedLocally: Frames saved on device — CSV log as database
settings.portalUrlHint: Point the app at your Geospector Portal to publish sessions directly from the Log tab. Leave blank if you are not using a portal.
settings.dynamicModeBody: In distance mode, the app uses live GPS speed to decide when to extract a frame. A frame is saved every time you travel the set distance — so you get consistent spatial coverage regardless of how fast you're moving.
settings.languageHint: Override the phone language for this app.

export.title: Export
export.fullArchiveDesc: Everything in one ZIP — all frames, GPS tracks, GeoJSON layer, and CSV database.
export.gisPackageDesc: Spatial data ready for QGIS, ArcGIS, Mapbox, or Google Earth. No photos — just the data layer.
export.inspectionPackageDesc: Photos with CSV metadata sidecar and GPS tracks — designed for site surveys, walk-arounds, and field inspections.
export.gpsTracksDesc: All session GPX route files bundled together. Import into navigation apps or GIS tools.
export.noGpxFound: No GPX track files found. Record routes in Manual mode using the Start GPX button.
export.geojsonDesc: Single FeatureCollection with every GPS-tagged frame as a point feature. Works in any modern GIS tool.
export.kmlDesc: Keyhole Markup Language — open directly in Google Earth, Google Maps, or any KML-compatible viewer.
export.csvDesc: Full frame log with timestamps, coordinates, session IDs, and file paths. Import into Excel, Sheets, or a database.
export.filesHint: Raw files are also accessible via the Files app under Geospector

upload.savedLocallyDesc: No cloud provider configured. Frames and CSV log are saved on your device. Configure a provider in Settings → Cloud Storage.
upload.offline: Offline — uploads will resume when connected
upload.noFramesCaptured: No detection frames were captured this session.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.message: Please reload the app to continue.

storage.preconfigured: Cloud storage is pre-configured by your administrator.
storage.preconfiguredSubtitle: This app has been set up with Supabase credentials by your administrator. No manual setup is required.
storage.overrideNote: These credentials are baked into the app build. You can override them by reconfiguring manually below.
storage.chooseSubtitle: Choose where to upload your captured frames.
storage.connectWithAccountDesc: Sign in to your account and pick a project — no credentials to copy
storage.supabaseManualDesc: Enter your Project URL, anon key, and bucket manually
storage.webhookDesc: POST frames as base64 to any HTTP endpoint
storage.patSubtitle: Enter your Supabase Personal Access Token to browse your projects.
storage.patTokenDetail:
It is kept in memory only during setup to fetch your project credentials, and is cleared when you close this screen.

Generate a token at
storage.enterNameBelow: Enter a name in the field below
storage.orExistingBucket: or use an existing bucket name
storage.bucketHint: The bucket must already exist in your Supabase project with public access or an anon-upload RLS policy.
storage.createInSupabase: Create a new bucket in Supabase ↗
storage.testingSubtitleSupabase: Connecting to your Supabase bucket, please wait.
storage.testingSubtitleWebhook: Connecting to your webhook endpoint, please wait.
storage.successSubtitleSupabase: Frames will upload to your Supabase bucket after each session. Uploads retry automatically if you go offline.
storage.successSubtitleWebhook: Frames will be POSTed to your endpoint after each session. Uploads retry automatically if you go offline.
storage.uploadQueuedNote: Uploads are queued and sent in the background. If the device goes offline, they resume automatically when connectivity is restored.
storage.errorHint: Check that your credentials are correct and that the bucket exists with public access or an anon-upload RLS policy.
storage.supabaseStep1: Go to supabase.com and create a project (or open an existing one).
storage.supabaseStep2a: In the left sidebar, open Storage → New Bucket.
storage.supabaseStep2b: Name it anything (e.g. 'frames'). Set the bucket to Public or configure an RLS policy that permits anon uploads.
storage.supabaseStep3: Go to Project Settings → API and copy:
storage.supabaseStep4: The app creates folder structure automatically — no manual setup needed:
storage.supabaseStep4Note: One folder per recording session (named by UUID).

storage.webhookStep2: The app sends a JSON body with these fields:
storage.webhookStep3: Respond with any 2xx status and optionally include:

map.notAvailableDesc: Open in Expo Go on your device to see GPS frames on the map.
map.noFramesDesc: Capture GPS-tagged frames to see them plotted here.

shareMap.title: Share Interactive Map
shareMap.descLocal: Generate a self-contained interactive map and share it as a file — recipient opens in any browser, no account needed.
shareMap.descSupabase: Upload an interactive map to Supabase Storage and share the public link — opens in any browser.
shareMap.descWebhook: Post session data to your webhook — recipient receives a browser-ready interactive map from your server.
shareMap.noPhotos: Route data only — no photos to embed
shareMap.capWarning: {{dropped}} photo(s) dropped to stay under 10 MB
shareMap.localDoneNote: Recipient opens the .html file in any browser to view the interactive map.
shareMap.urlNote: Opens as a full interactive map in any browser.
shareMap.sentNoUrl: Sent — server did not return a link.
shareMap.sentNoUrlNote: The operator’s server controls whether a share URL is provided.
shareMap.noResults: No frames match the current filter
